inputs.declared_question: Which execution assumptions belong inside a generative plate, and which should remain replaceable properties of a reader?

sources_checked.title: Field Note 33: The Plate and the Pull

source_facts.claim: The core standard defines a safe, portable, low-level code format with validation and execution semantics, while leaving the surrounding environment to an embedder.

The JavaScript Interface specifies construction and instantiation of modules, imported and exported calls, data exchange, and errors across that embedding boundary. Its current draft is dated 11 September 2026.
Field Note 33 proposes a public generative algorithm, a recognized edition lineage, and an encounter on a visitor's machine without a sole renderer or catalog service.

cartographer.inference: A portable computation and explicit embedding boundary remain a possible technical adjacency to the replaceable reader in FN-33, not a substitute for its art assets, intended rendering, edition lineage, or authority to end the edition.
cartographer.uncertainty: The September JavaScript Interface update does not, by itself, change the already proposed core relation; it does not establish cross-environment visual determinism or preservation of a whole artwork.
cartographer.attribution: External facts come from official W3C public specifications. No external person or organization was contacted, and no private material was read.
cartographer.no_proposal_reason: The official sources continue to support the existing proposed node and cautious technical adjacency. A new candidate would duplicate the map.

decisions.decision: Retain the possible WebAssembly technical adjacency and its explicit limits.
Leave the three-item Attending arrangement unchanged; catalog evidence repair does not warrant a public relational turn.
